definition_en: a great flood or heavy rain, or a huge amount of something arriving at once
core_image: 河水漫过堤岸，街道变成水道，邮箱里同时塞进上百封未读邮件
scene: 洪水冲毁了那座老桥。The deluge destroyed the old bridge.

pos.zh: 洪水；暴雨；大量涌来的事物
淹没；使充斥；使应接不暇

senses.title: Great flood
senses.definition: a great flood of water covering land that is usually dry
senses.definitionCN: 淹没平时干燥土地的大水
senses.example: The deluge destroyed the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水冲毁了那座老桥。
senses.why: A river climbing over its own bank.
senses.whyCN: 一条爬过自己堤岸的河。

senses.title: Heavy rain
senses.definition: a very heavy fall of rain
senses.definitionCN: 极大的降雨
senses.example: We were caught in a deluge on the moor.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在荒地上遇上了暴雨。
senses.why: Rain falling faster than the gutters can take it.
senses.whyCN: 雨落得比排水沟能承受的更快。

senses.title: A flood of things
senses.definition: a huge amount of something arriving at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物同时涌来
senses.example: The office was deluged with complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室被投诉淹没了。
senses.why: An inbox with a hundred unread lines.
senses.whyCN: 一个有一百条未读的收件箱。

intro.en: Deluge comes from Latin diluvium, a great flood, from diluere, to wash away.
intro.cn: deluge 源自拉丁语 diluvium（大洪水），后者来自 diluere（冲走）。

items.en: Luere meant to wash or wash away.
items.cn: luere 意为洗、冲走。

items.en: Diluere meant to wash away or dissolve.
items.cn: diluere 意为冲走、溶解。

items.en: Diluvium named a great flood.
items.cn: diluvium 指大洪水。

items.en: Deluge entered English through Old French for the biblical flood.
items.cn: 十四世纪 deluge 经古法语进入英语，指圣经中的大洪水。

items.en: It widened to any overwhelming downpour or rush.
items.cn: 十七世纪扩展到任何压倒性的暴雨或涌来。

items.en: It is now common for floods of mail and requests.
items.cn: 如今常用于邮件与请求的洪流。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the lu- washing and playing family; the near-meaning group names things that arrive in overwhelming amounts.
note.cn: 形近组共享 lu-（冲、戏）家族；近义组都是「量大到压倒」的说法。

normalIntro.cn: deluge 就是把一切冲走的水：一条河、一场暴雨，或一次涌来的一百封邮件。

normal.en: Be deluged with work means too much work at once.

definition_zh: n. 错觉；妄想；欺骗；迷惑
definition_en: a false belief that is firmly held, or the act of deceiving someone
core_image: 一个人坚信镜子里的人是别人，医生的记录本上写着「与现实不符」
scene: 那种被人跟踪的想法是妄想。The idea of being followed was a delusion.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：delusion 指妄想；句意是那种被人跟踪的想法是一种妄想。

pos.zh: 错觉；妄想；欺骗；迷惑

senses.title: False belief
senses.definition: a belief that is not true but is firmly held
senses.definitionCN: 不真实却被坚信的想法
senses.example: She was under the delusion that he would return.
senses.exampleCN: 她错以为他会回来。
senses.why: A map drawn from a wish, not a survey.
senses.whyCN: 一张凭愿望而非测量画出的地图。

senses.title: Clinical symptom
senses.definition: a fixed false belief that persists despite evidence, as in illness
senses.definitionCN: 尽管有相反证据仍固定不变的错误信念，如疾病中的症状
senses.example: The idea of being followed was a delusion.
senses.exampleCN: 那种被人跟踪的想法是一种妄想。
senses.why: A locked door checked five times an hour.
senses.whyCN: 一小时被检查五次的门锁。

senses.title: Act of deceiving
senses.definition: the act of misleading someone about what is true
senses.definitionCN: 就真相误导他人的行为
senses.example: The whole scheme was a delusion of the public.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划是对公众的欺骗。
senses.why: A stage mirror that hides the wire.
senses.whyCN: 一面藏起钢丝的舞台镜子。

intro.en: Delusion comes from Latin deludere, de- plus ludere, to play or mock: to play a trick on the mind.
intro.cn: delusion 源自拉丁语 deludere，由 de- 加 ludere（玩耍、嘲弄）构成：拿心智开玩笑。

items.en: Ludere meant to play or to mock.
items.cn: ludere 意为玩耍、嘲弄。

items.en: Deludere meant to mock or deceive.
items.cn: deludere 意为嘲弄、欺骗。

items.en: Delusio named a deceiving or a mockery.
items.cn: delusio 指欺骗或嘲弄。

items.en: Delusion entered English for a false belief.
items.cn: 十五世纪 delusion 以错误信念义进入英语。

items.en: Psychiatry made it a technical symptom term.
items.cn: 十九世纪精神医学把它变成专业症状术语。

items.en: It is used loosely for any self-deception.
items.cn: 如今泛指任何自我欺骗。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the lud- playing family; the near-meaning group names other ways the mind goes wrong.
note.cn: 形近组共享 lud-（玩）家族；近义组是心智出错的其他方式。

entries.definition: To make someone believe something false.
A hint at something without naming it.
Something that looks real but is not.
The act of making someone believe what is false.
An idea that is mistaken.
Seeing or hearing something that is not there.

normalIntro.en: Delusion is de- plus lud- play: the mind has been played a trick on and believes it.
normalIntro.cn: delusion 就是 de- 加 lud-（玩）：心智被耍了一招，还信以为真。

normal.en: Lud- means to play, as in ludicrous.
normal.cn: lud- 意为玩，如 ludicrous。

normal.en: De- here means badly.
normal.cn: 这里 de- 表示坏。

normal.en: A delusion is a belief the facts refuse.
normal.cn: delusion 是事实拒绝支持的信念。

normal.en: Delusions of grandeur make a man feel like a king.
normal.cn: 夸大妄想让人自以为是国王。

normal.en: Illusion tricks the eye; delusion tricks the belief.
normal.cn: illusion 骗眼睛，delusion 骗信念。

examples.en: He suffers from delusions of grandeur.
examples.cn: 他有夸大妄想。

examples.en: The delusion collapsed when the letter arrived.
examples.cn: 信一到，错觉就破灭了。

examples.en: They were labouring under a delusion.
examples.cn: 他们一直抱着一个错误的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: delusion 谐音「弟路申」——不如记 de（坏）＋ lus（玩弄，与 illusion 同根 ludere）＋ ion＝认知被人玩弄了，「错觉、妄想」。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一幅假图景：一个愿望、一个症状与一场把戏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man sure the person in the mirror is someone else, the notes saying it does not match reality

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ludere 意为玩，deludere 意为欺骗，capere 意为拿。

definition_zh: 要求；需求；需要
definition_en: to ask for something firmly, or the need that people have for a thing
core_image: 一只手伸到柜台前，掌心向上，等着对方把东西递过来
scene: 柜台前排队的人越来越多，店员却只有两个，队伍里开始有人提高声音。The workers demanded a clear answer about their pay.
sceneCN: 这里 demand 指「要求」（第 1 个义项：坚决地提出要求）；句意是工人们要求就工资给出明确答复。

pos.zh: 要求；强烈请求；需要
需求；要求

senses.title: Ask for something firmly
senses.definition: to ask for something in a strong way that expects an answer
senses.definitionCN: 以强硬、期待答复的方式提出要求
senses.example: The workers demanded a clear answer about their pay.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求就工资给出明确答复。
senses.why: A request becomes a demand when the asker will not take silence for an answer.
senses.whyCN: 当提问者不肯把沉默当作答复时，请求就变成了要求。

senses.title: The need for a product
senses.definition: the amount of a product or service that people want to buy
senses.definitionCN: 人们想购买的产品或服务的数量
senses.example: There is a growing demand for small electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 小型电动汽车的需求在增长。
senses.why: Want becomes demand when it is strong enough to reach the market.
senses.whyCN: 当想要的力度大到愿意掏钱，想要就成了需求。

senses.title: Need time or effort
senses.definition: to need a particular quality, time or effort in order to be done
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事需要某种品质、时间或精力
senses.example: Learning a language demands patience.
senses.exampleCN: 学一门语言需要耐心。
senses.why: Some tasks ask for qualities the way people ask for help.
senses.whyCN: 有些任务索要品质，就像人开口求助一样。

intro.en: Demand reached English through Old French, but its parts are Latin: de- meaning fully and mandare meaning to hand over or order.
intro.cn: demand 经古法语进入英语，零件却是拉丁的：de- 表示完全，mandare 表示交付或命令。

items.en: Demandare joined de-, meaning fully, to mandare, to hand over or order.
items.cn: demandare 由 de-（完全）与 mandare（交付、命令）合成。

items.en: Demander could ask a question or make a claim in court.
items.cn: demander 既可以提问，也可以在法庭上提出主张。

items.en: English borrowed it as both a verb of asking and a noun of claim.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，既作表示询问的动词，也作表示主张的名词。

items.en: Economists gave the noun its sense of want backed by money.
items.cn: 经济学家给这个名词添上了「有购买力的想要」这一层。

items.en: Today it covers both a firm request and the pull of the market.
items.cn: 如今它既指坚决的请求，也指市场的拉动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -mand sound, and the meaning group moves from a polite request to a legal claim.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -mand 这一段音，近义组则从礼貌请求一路走到法律上的主张。

entries.definition: to order someone to do something
needing a lot of time and effort
entries.definitionCN: 需要大量时间与精力的

entries.definition: a person who asks for something
to ask for something in a polite way
to need something or make it necessary
entries.definitionCN: 需要某物或使其成为必要

entries.definition: to say that something belongs to you

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand held out at a counter and end with a market that keeps pulling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从柜台前伸出的一只手开始，落到一个不停拉动的市场。

normal.en: A hand held out and not pulled back is already a demand.
normal.cn: 一只手伸出去不收回，就已经是要求了。

normal.en: In a shop, want becomes demand when the money is ready.
normal.cn: 在店里，钱准备好了，想要就变成了需求。

normal.en: A task can demand patience the way a customer demands service.
normal.cn: 任务索要耐心，就像顾客索要服务。

normal.en: Two curves meet on a chart: one asks, one answers.
normal.cn: 两条曲线在图上相遇：一条发问，一条回答。

normal.en: Demand and command share a spine; one asks, one orders.
normal.cn: demand 与 command 共用一副骨架：一个请求，一个命令。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that grows longer while the counter stays the same.
abstract.cn: 想象队伍越来越长，柜台却始终只有那么大。

abstract.en: Picture an empty shelf with a note saying sold out.
abstract.cn: 想象一排空货架，上面贴着售罄的纸条。

abstract.en: Picture a palm turned upward and fingers closing slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一只掌心向上的手，手指慢慢收拢。

examples.en: The workers demanded a clear answer about their pay.
examples.cn: 工人们要求就工资给出明确答复。

examples.en: There is a growing demand for small electric cars.
examples.cn: 小型电动汽车的需求在增长。

examples.en: Learning a language demands patience and daily practice.
examples.cn: 学一门语言需要耐心和每日练习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 demand 记成「得忙的」：de 像「得」，mand 像「忙的」，订单一来，全厂都得忙起来，这就是要求与需求。

root: 来自拉丁语 demandare，由 de-（完全）与 mandare（交付、命令）组成，经古法语 demander 进入英语。它先是郑重地提出要求，后来又分出经济上的需求，也用来表示事情对时间与精力的索求。

sensesIntro.en: From a firm request at a counter, to the pull of the market, to the effort a task asks of you.
sensesIntro.cn: 从柜台前一句坚决的请求，到市场的拉动，再到任务向你要的时间与力气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm held out and waiting at a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只掌心向上的手在柜台前等着。

branches.en: The first sense is a request that expects an answer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是期待答复的请求。

branches.en: When many people want the same thing, the wish becomes a market force.
branches.cn: 当许多人都想要同一样东西，愿望就成了市场力量。

branches.en: A task can also ask, and what it asks for is time or patience.
branches.cn: 任务也会开口，它要的是时间或耐心。

branches.en: A firm request and a market need both push against the world.
branches.cn: 坚决的请求与市场的需要，都在向世界施压。

branches.en: Both the market and a hard task measure how much people will give.
branches.cn: 市场与艰难的任务都在衡量人愿意付出多少。

intro.en: Demand forms a small family around asking, needing and the side of the market that wants goods.
intro.cn: demand 长出一小族词，围绕请求、需要以及市场中想要货物的一方。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is mandare, to hand over or order, with de- adding fullness.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 mandare（交付、命令），前缀 de- 加上了完全的意思。

items.meaning: to ask firmly, or a need

items.exampleCN: 那是一份要求很高的工作。
提出要求的人在外面等。

items.meaning: relating to buyers in a market
items.exampleCN: 他们研究了需求侧的影响。

items.meaning: a line showing how much people will buy

items.exampleCN: 她是一位抢手的设计师。

items.meaning: in a way that asks for much

definition_zh: n. 痴呆；失智症（记忆与思维能力的严重衰退）
definition_en: a serious loss of memory and thinking ability, usually in old age
core_image: 一位老人握着钥匙站在门口，却想不起这扇门通向哪里，日历上的名字被反复描过
scene: 照护中心为痴呆患者设计了标识。The centre designed signs for people with dementia.
sceneCN: 第 3 个义项：dementia 指这一类疾病；句意是照护中心为痴呆患者设计了标识。

pos.zh: 痴呆；失智症

senses.title: Loss of memory
senses.definition: a decline in memory severe enough to disrupt daily life
senses.definitionCN: 严重到影响日常生活的记忆衰退
senses.example: Dementia made the names of her grandchildren slip away.
senses.exampleCN: 痴呆让她记不起孙辈的名字。
senses.why: A key held at a door that no longer feels familiar.
senses.whyCN: 一把握在门口、却不再觉得熟悉的钥匙。

senses.title: Loss of thinking
senses.definition: a decline in judgement, planning and language
senses.definitionCN: 判断、计划与语言能力的衰退
senses.example: The dementia made paying bills impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 痴呆让他无法付账单。
senses.why: A calendar with the same name written over and over.
senses.whyCN: 一本同一个名字被反复描写的日历。

senses.title: A group of diseases
senses.definition: the family of conditions, such as Alzheimer disease, that cause this decline
senses.definitionCN: 导致这种衰退的一类疾病，如阿尔茨海默病
senses.example: The centre designed signs for people with dementia.
senses.exampleCN: 照护中心为痴呆患者设计了标识。
senses.why: A ward where every door carries a picture cue.
senses.whyCN: 一间每扇门都贴着图片提示的病房。

intro.en: Dementia is Latin de-, away, plus mens, mind, plus -ia, a condition: the mind gone away.
intro.cn: dementia 由拉丁语 de-（离开）加 mens（心智）加 -ia（病症）构成：心智离开了。

items.en: Mens meant the mind in Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智。

items.en: Dementia meant being out of the mind.
items.cn: dementia 意为失去心智。

items.en: Doctors used dementia for acquired mental loss.
items.cn: 医生用 dementia 指后天获得的心智丧失。

items.en: It became a category distinct from lifelong conditions.
items.cn: 它成为与终身性疾病相区别的一个类别。

intro.en: Democratic adds the Greek adjective ending -ic to democrat, which comes from demos, the people, and kratia, rule.
intro.cn: democratic 是 democrat 加上希腊形容词词尾 -ic；democrat 由 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）组成。

items.en: Demokratia joined demos, the people, with kratia, rule.
items.cn: demokratia 由 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）合成。

items.en: Athenian writers used demokratikos for things belonging to popular rule.
items.cn: 雅典作家用 demokratikos 形容属于民众统治的事物。

items.en: Latin authors borrowed the Greek adjective in discussions of constitutions.
items.cn: 拉丁作家在讨论政体时借用了这个希腊形容词。

items.en: English formed democratic to describe power held by the people.
items.cn: 英语造出 democratic，用来形容由人民掌握的权力。

items.en: Today it also describes any group that shares decisions fairly.
items.cn: 如今它也形容任何公平分享决定的群体。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the demo- opening, and the meaning group offers words for equal power and for standing in for others.
note.cn: 形近组都以 demo- 开头，近义组则给出表示平等权力与代表他人的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a circle of chairs and end with a decision that no single person could make alone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一圈椅子开始，落到一个谁也独自做不出的决定。

normal.en: A circle of chairs has no head and no foot.
normal.cn: 围成一圈的椅子，没有头也没有尾。

normal.en: If one hand is always the only one raised, the room is not democratic.
normal.cn: 如果永远只有一只手举起，这间屋子就不民主。

normal.en: The word carries a Greek crowd inside it.
normal.cn: 这个词里装着一群希腊人。

normal.en: A vote in a classroom is small, but the habit is the same size as a nation.
normal.cn: 教室里的投票很小，习惯却和一个国家一样大。

normal.en: Demo- means people, so democratic means the people hold the pen.

abstract.en: Picture a hand count where every arm moves at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象一次举手表决，所有手臂同时抬起。

abstract.en: Picture a rule book with one page that says no one is above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册，其中一页写着没有人高过它。

abstract.en: Picture a small club where the leader also washes the cups.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小社团，负责人也要去洗杯子。

examples.en: The country held its first democratic election in decades.
examples.cn: 这个国家举行了几十年来第一次民主选举。

examples.en: The club made a democratic decision to share the work equally.

examples.en: A democratic classroom lets students disagree with the teacher.
examples.cn: 民主的课堂允许学生不同意老师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 democratic 记成「得摸克拉提克」：demo 是人民，crat 是统治，ic 是形容词尾，人民统治的，就是民主的。

root: 来自希腊语 demokratikos，由 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）再加形容词词尾 -ic 构成，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。它本指与人民统治有关的事物，后来也用来形容任何讲究平等参与的做法。

sensesIntro.en: From a nation that counts its votes, to a small room where every member counts once.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个清点选票的国家，到一间每个成员都只算一票的小屋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of chairs where no seat is higher than another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈椅子，没有哪一张比别的更高。

branches.en: The first sense is a state whose power starts with votes.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是权力起始于选票的国家。

branches.en: The second sense is a room where every member counts once.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是每个成员都只算一票的屋子。

branches.en: A country and a club share the same test: who gets to speak.
branches.cn: 国家与社团面对同一道考题：谁有资格说话。

branches.en: The word also says who the power belongs to: the people, not a family.
branches.cn: 这个词也说明权力属于谁：属于人民，不属于某个家族。

branches.en: Used in small groups, it simply means no one sits above the vote.
branches.cn: 用在小组里，它只是说没有人坐在投票之上。

intro.en: Democratic grows a family of nouns and verbs about rule by the people and the act of opening a group to all.
intro.cn: democratic 长出一族名词与动词，讲人民统治，也讲把一个群体向所有人打开。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base is demos, the people, joined to kratia, rule, and then to the Latin adjective ending -ic.

senses.title: Relating to population structure
senses.definition: connected with the size, age and make-up of a population
senses.definitionCN: 与人口的规模、年龄与构成有关
senses.example: Demographic change has left more pensioners than children.
senses.exampleCN: 人口结构变化使领取养老金的人多于儿童。
senses.why: dēmos 'people' plus graphein 'write' gives the study of populations, and the adjective simply describes whatever belongs to that study.
senses.whyCN: dēmos「民众」加 graphein「书写」构成对人口的研究，形容词就描述属于这项研究的一切。

senses.title: Relating to population statistics
senses.definition: connected with the numbers collected about births, deaths, migration and age
senses.definitionCN: 与出生、死亡、迁移与年龄等收集到的数字有关
senses.example: The report opens with a demographic table by region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告开头是一张分地区的人口统计表。
senses.why: the adjective covers both the structure and the figures, so it can sit before data as easily as before change.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词同时涵盖结构与数字，因此既能修饰 change，也能修饰 data。

senses.title: A group with shared traits
senses.titleCN: 由共同特征界定的人群（名词义）
senses.definition: a section of a population defined by age, income, education or similar traits
senses.definitionCN: 按年龄、收入、教育等特征划分出来的一部分人口
senses.example: The survey split respondents by demographic group before comparing answers.
senses.exampleCN: 调查先把受访者按人口特征分组，再比较答案。
senses.why: marketers needed a countable slice of the population, so the adjective became a noun naming that slice.
senses.whyCN: 营销需要人口中可数的一块，于是形容词转为名词，命名那一块。

senses.title: The collected figures
senses.definition: the statistics themselves, usually in the plural demographics
senses.definitionCN: 指统计数字本身，通常用复数 demographics
senses.example: The demographics show a young city growing older.
senses.exampleCN: 统计数据显示，一座年轻的城市正在变老。
senses.why: once the figures are habitually referred to in the plural, demographics becomes a noun in its own right.
senses.whyCN: 当这些数字习惯上用复数指称，demographics 就独立成为名词。

senses.title: The transition model
senses.titleCN: 人口转变模型中的用法
senses.definition: belonging to the model that traces a society from high to low birth and death rates
senses.definitionCN: 属于描述社会由高出生高死亡转向低出生低死亡的模式
senses.example: Demographic transition explains the lag between falling deaths and falling births.
senses.exampleCN: 人口转变解释了死亡下降与出生下降之间的时间差。
senses.why: the model needed a fixed name, and the adjective supplied one that fits every stage of the shift.
senses.whyCN: 模式需要一个固定名称，这个形容词正好提供一个能套住各阶段的名称。

senses.title: A dividend from age structure
senses.titleCN: 人口红利：劳动年龄人口占比高带来的增益
senses.definition: the economic gain a country receives when working-age adults outnumber dependants
senses.definitionCN: 劳动年龄成年人多于受抚养者时，国家获得的经济增益
senses.example: The demographic dividend lasted two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 人口红利持续了二十年。
senses.why: economists priced the age structure, so a bulge of workers became a dividend to be spent.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家给年龄结构定了价，于是劳动力高峰成了一份可以花掉的红利。

senses.title: Ageing and shrinking
senses.definition: belonging to the trend of older populations and fewer births
senses.definitionCN: 属于人口老化、出生减少的趋势
senses.example: Demographic ageing is reshaping the labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化正在重塑劳动力市场。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to any trend defined by the age profile, and ageing is now the dominant one.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可接任何由年龄结构定义的走势，而老龄化如今是主要那一个。

senses.title: A market segment label
senses.definition: used by business to describe the slice of customers a product is aimed at
senses.definitionCN: 商业用来描述产品针对的那一部分顾客
senses.example: The app was built for a younger demographic.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用是为更年轻的人群打造的。
senses.why: segmentation turned the adjective into a targeting word, and the noun became shorthand for the audience itself.
senses.whyCN: 市场细分把这个形容词变成定向用词，名词则成了受众本身的简称。

intro.en: Demographic combines Greek dēmos 'the people' with -graphic from graphein 'to write'. Demography was coined in 1855 by Achille Guillard. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: demographic 把希腊 dēmos「民众」与来自 graphein「书写」的 -graphic 结合。demography 由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dēmos meant 'the people, the common people' and also named a district; it is the root of democracy as well as demography.
items.cn: dēmos 意为「民众、平民」，也指一个行政区；它既是 demography 的词根，也是 democracy 的词根。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, to draw'; with -ia it made words for a field of writing or study, as in geography.
items.cn: graphein 意为「书写、刻画」；加 -ia 构成表示某一书写或研究领域的词，如 geography。

items.en: The noun demography is generally credited to Achille Guillard, who used démographie in a work of 1855.
items.cn: 名词 demography 一般归功于 Achille Guillard，他在 1855 年的一部著作中使用了 démographie。

items.en: The adjective demographic followed in the later nineteenth century, and the plural noun demographics spread in the twentieth as market research grew.
items.cn: 形容词 demographic 在 19 世纪后期出现；复数名词 demographics 随 20 世纪市场研究的发展而扩散。

items.en: The twentieth century added fixed phrases such as demographic transition and demographic dividend, turning the word into a policy instrument.
items.cn: 20 世纪又增添了 demographic transition 与 demographic dividend 等固定说法，使这个词成为政策工具。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English use of the adjective is not precisely recorded, and the exact month of Guillard's coinage is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词在英语中的最早使用没有精确记录；Guillard 造词的确切月份亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same demo- and -graphy stock that are constantly swapped; group two holds terms for describing groups of people.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 demo- 与 -graphy 词干、常被互换的词；第二组是描述人群的其他术语。

entries.definitionCN: 泛指与统计有关；demographic 把它限定到人口数字。

entries.definition: Combining social and economic position; demographic covers age and household too.
entries.definitionCN: 结合社会与经济地位；demographic 还涵盖年龄与家庭。

root: 希腊 dēmos「民众、平民」+ graphein「书写」（经 -graphic）；demography 由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出。英语 demographic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one view: a population is drawn as a chart, and that view is then read as structure, statistics, a targeted segment, a data set, a transition, a dividend, an ageing trend and a market label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种视角展开：把人口画成图表，这个视角再被读成结构、统计、定向人群、数据集、转变、红利、老化趋势与市场标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a population pyramid, wide at the base and narrow at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座底宽顶尖的人口金字塔。

branches.en: THE VIEW ITSELF: what belongs to population structure and to its figures.
branches.cn: 视角本身：属于人口结构与统计数字的东西。

branches.en: A SLICE OF PEOPLE: the adjective becomes a countable segment and then a market target.
branches.cn: 人群的一小块：形容词变成可数的人群，再变成市场目标。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: demographics as a plural noun for collected figures.
branches.cn: 数字本身：demographics 作复数名词指收集到的数据。

branches.en: MODEL AND GAIN: the transition describes change, the dividend prices it.
branches.cn: 模型与增益：转变描述变化，红利为其定价。

branches.en: AGEING TREND: older populations and fewer births become a standing phrase.
branches.cn: 老化趋势：人口变老与出生减少成为固定说法。

intro.en: Demographic is built from two Greek elements; demo- is a combining form and -graphic a suffix meaning 'written or described'.
intro.cn: demographic 由两个希腊成分构成；demo- 是组合形式，-graphic 是表示「书写、描绘」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek rather than Latin: dēmos 'people' and graphein 'to write', the second also giving geography and biography.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个成分属希腊语而非拉丁语：dēmos「民众」与 graphein「书写」，后者还构成 geography 与 biography。

definition_zh: 人口学；人口统计
definition_en: the statistical study of populations, especially births, deaths and migration
core_image: 一本登记册上并排列着出生、死亡、迁入、迁出四栏，数字逐年累积
scene: 人口登记册摊在桌上，四栏数字逐年累积：Demography tracks births, deaths and migration across a whole region.
sceneCN: 这里 demography 指「以统计方法研究人口的学科」（第 1 个义项：系统记录与分析出生、死亡与迁移）；句意为人口学追踪整个地区的出生、死亡与迁移。图中可辨识物件：四栏登记册、逐年累积的数字、区域地图、统计笔。

pos.zh: 人口学；人口统计（不可数；指数据时偶用复数 demographics）

derivatives.zh: 人口统计的 / 特定人群

senses.title: The statistical study of populations
senses.definition: the discipline that measures and analyses the size, structure and change of populations
senses.definitionCN: 测量与分析人口规模、结构与变化的学科
senses.example: Demography tracks births, deaths and migration across a whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 人口学追踪整个地区的出生、死亡与迁移。
senses.why: dēmos 'people' plus graphein 'write' names a field defined by writing down the people, and the modern discipline is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: dēmos「民众」加 graphein「书写」命名了一个「把民众写下来」的领域，现代学科正是如此。

senses.title: The data it produces
senses.titleCN: 该学科产出的统计数据
senses.definition: the body of figures about a population produced by that study
senses.definitionCN: 该研究产生的关于人口的整套数字
senses.example: The demography of the valley is recorded parish by parish.
senses.exampleCN: 这条谷地的人口数据按教区逐一记录。
senses.why: the discipline and its output share one name, so demography can mean either the study or the record it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 学科与产物共用一个名称，因此 demography 既可指研究，也可指它留下的记录。

senses.title: Formal demography
senses.titleCN: 形式人口学：只算出生死亡迁移
senses.definition: the branch that works with births, deaths and migration alone, without social explanation
senses.definitionCN: 只处理出生、死亡与迁移、不作社会解释的分支
senses.example: Formal demography can show the change but not why it happened.
senses.exampleCN: 形式人口学能显示变化，却不能说明原因。
senses.why: counting needs a boundary, and the formal branch draws it at births, deaths and migration only.
senses.whyCN: 计数需要一条边界，形式分支就把它画在出生、死亡与迁移这三处。

senses.title: Social demography
senses.titleCN: 社会人口学：把人口与社会结构连起来
senses.definition: the branch that connects population patterns with class, family and culture
senses.definitionCN: 把人口格局与阶层、家庭、文化联系起来的分支
senses.example: Social demography asks who can afford to have children.
senses.exampleCN: 社会人口学问的是谁养得起孩子。
senses.why: once the counting is secure, the next question is explanation, and social demography brings class and family back in.
senses.whyCN: 一旦计数可靠，下一个问题就是解释，社会人口学把阶层与家庭带回来。

senses.title: Historical demography
senses.titleCN: 历史人口学：重建过去的人口
senses.definition: the branch that reconstructs past populations from registers and records
senses.definitionCN: 从登记簿与档案重建过去人口的分支
senses.example: Historical demography rebuilt the parish from baptism records.
senses.exampleCN: 历史人口学靠洗礼记录重建了这个教区的人口。
senses.why: where no census survives, registers become the data, and the same methods are applied backwards in time.
senses.whyCN: 在没有普查留存的年代，登记簿成了数据，同一套方法被倒推回过去。

senses.title: Business demography
senses.definition: the use of population analysis to describe customers and markets
senses.definitionCN: 用人口分析描述顾客与市场
senses.example: Business demography showed the brand ageing with its buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 商业人口分析显示这个品牌随顾客一起变老。
senses.why: customers can be counted like a population, so market research borrows the field without changing its methods.
senses.whyCN: 顾客可以像人口一样计数，因此市场研究借用了这门学科而不改其方法。

senses.title: Applied demography
senses.titleCN: 应用人口学：服务规划与政策
senses.definition: the use of demographic methods for planning schools, housing and pensions
senses.definitionCN: 把人口方法用于学校、住房与养老金规划
senses.example: Applied demography projected how many classrooms the county needs.
senses.exampleCN: 应用人口学预测了这个县需要多少间教室。
senses.why: planning needs projections rather than descriptions, so the applied branch turns the method into a forecast.
senses.whyCN: 规划需要预测而非描述，应用分支就把方法变成一份预报。

senses.title: Demography of other species
senses.titleCN: 生态学义：其他物种的种群统计
senses.definition: the study of births, deaths and movement in non-human populations
senses.definitionCN: 研究非人类种群的出生、死亡与移动
senses.example: The demography of the wolves is followed by radio collars.
senses.exampleCN: 狼群的种群统计靠无线电项圈追踪。
senses.why: the four columns work for any species, so ecology uses the same word for packs and herds.
senses.whyCN: 那四栏账对任何物种都适用，因此生态学用同一个词指兽群与畜群。

intro.en: Demography joins Greek dēmos 'people' to -graphy from graphein 'to write'; the word was coined in 1855 by Achille Guillard. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: demography 把希腊 dēmos「民众」与来自 graphein「书写」的 -graphy 结合；该词由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dēmos named the people of a town or district; it survives in democracy, epidemic and demography.
items.cn: dēmos 指一城或一区的民众；它留存于 democracy、epidemic 与 demography 中。

items.en: Graphein 'to write' produced -graphia, a suffix for description or a field of study, as in geography.
items.cn: graphein「书写」产生 -graphia，即表示描述或研究领域的后缀，如 geography。

items.en: Achille Guillard introduced démographie in 1855 in a work on human statistics, defining it as the natural and social history of the human species.
items.cn: Achille Guillard 于 1855 年在一部人类统计著作中提出 démographie，并把它界定为人类的自然史与社会史。

items.en: English adopted demography in the later nineteenth century, and the adjective demographic followed.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪后期吸收 demography，形容词 demographic 随后出现。

items.en: The twentieth century split the field into formal, social, historical and applied branches with their own methods.
items.cn: 20 世纪该领域分为形式、社会、历史与应用等分支，各有方法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation of demography is not precisely recorded, and the exact wording of Guillard's definition has variant translations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：demography 在英语中的最早书证没有精确记录；Guillard 定义的确切措辞存在不同译本。

note.en: Group one holds the demo- family members that are routinely confused; group two holds neighbouring fields and instruments.
note.cn: 第一组是 demo- 词族中常被混淆的成员；第二组是相邻的学科与工具。

entries.definition: The plural noun for population figures or segments; demography is the field that produces them.
entries.definitionCN: 复数名词，指人口数字或人群构成；demography 是产出它们的学科。

entries.definition: The adjective belonging to the field, also used as a countable noun for a segment.
entries.definitionCN: 属于该领域的形容词，也可作可数名词指某一人群。

entries.definition: A person who practises demography; the word names a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事人口学工作的人；命名一种职业。

entries.definition: The study of the earth and its peoples; it shares the -graphy ending but not the demo- root.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球及其人群的学科；共享 -graphy 结尾，但词根不是 demo-。

entries.definition: An umbrella term covering demography together with sociology and economics of population.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖人口学及人口社会学、人口经济学的总称。

entries.definition: The periodic official count; demography uses census data along with registers and surveys.
entries.definitionCN: 指定期官方清点；人口学除普查外还使用登记与抽样。

entries.definition: The general mathematics of data; demography applies it to populations specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指数据数学方法；人口学把它专门用于人口。

entries.definition: The study of disease in populations; it shares dēmos with demography but tracks illness, not births.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人群中疾病的学科；与人口学共享 dēmos，但追踪疾病而非出生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: demo- 'people' + -graphy 'writing': writing down the people.
normal.cn: demo-「民众」+ -graphy「书写」：把民众写下来。

normal.en: The family runs demography, demographer, demographic, demographics, demographically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 demography、demographer、demographic、demographics、demographically。

normal.en: The branches are formal, social, historical and applied.
normal.cn: 分支包括形式、社会、历史与应用四类。

normal.en: Coined in 1855 by Achille Guillard, which is why the word feels nineteenth-century.
normal.cn: 由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出，因此这个词带着 19 世纪的气息。

normal.en: Formal demography counts; social demography explains.
normal.cn: 形式人口学负责计数，社会人口学负责解释。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with four columns: born, died, arrived, left.
abstract.cn: 想象一本四栏账簿：出生、死亡、迁入、迁出。

abstract.en: Picture a village reconstructed from baptism ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一个靠洗礼墨水重建起来的村庄。

abstract.en: Picture a school board asking how many desks in ten years.
abstract.cn: 想象校董会在问十年后要多少张课桌。

examples.en: Demography shows the parish losing a generation.
examples.cn: 人口统计显示这个教区正在失去一代人。

examples.en: She teaches demography at the university.
examples.cn: 她在大学教人口学。

examples.en: The demography of the forest changed after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾之后，这片森林的种群统计发生了变化。

root: 希腊 dēmos「民众」+ graphein「书写」（经 -graphy）；1855 年由 Achille Guillard 造出，属希腊语复合，非拉丁词根。英语 demography。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practice: births, deaths and movement are written down, and the practice is then read as a discipline, a body of data, four branches and an ecological tool.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种做法展开：把出生、死亡与移动写下来，这个做法再被读成学科、数据集、四个分支与一种生态工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger with four columns filling year by year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本四栏账簿逐年填满。

branches.en: FIELD AND FORMAL CORE: the discipline first, then its narrowest counting branch.
branches.cn: 学科与形式核心：先是学科，再是最窄的计数分支。

branches.en: THE RECORD: the word also names the data written down.
branches.cn: 记录本身：这个词也指被写下的数据。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND HISTORICAL: explanation and reconstruction are the two wider branches.
branches.cn: 社会与历史：解释与重建是两个更宽的分支。

branches.en: APPLIED USE: business and planning both borrow the methods.
branches.cn: 应用：商业与规划都借用这套方法。

branches.en: OTHER SPECIES: wolves get the same four columns.
branches.cn: 其他物种：狼也用同样的四栏账。

intro.en: Demography is a Greek compound of a combining form and a suffix, with no Latin elements in its base.
intro.cn: demography 是希腊语的组合形式加后缀构成的复合词，基底不含拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here: dēmos 'people' and graphein 'to write' are Greek, and the same suffix built geography and biography.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：dēmos「民众」与 graphein「书写」都是希腊语，同一后缀还构成 geography 与 biography。

definition_zh: v. 拆除，拆毁（建筑）；推翻（论点）；彻底击败；（口语）吃光
definition_en: to pull down a building, or to destroy an argument or defeat someone completely
core_image: 挖掘机的臂杆撞上旧楼外墙，砖块一层层落下，地上只剩一圈地基
scene: 工人拆掉了那座旧仓库。The workers demolished the old warehouse.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：demolished 指拆除；句意是工人拆掉了那座旧仓库。

pos.zh: 拆除，拆毁；推翻（论点）；彻底击败；（口语）吃光

senses.title: Pull down a building
senses.definition: to knock down or pull apart a building or structure
senses.definitionCN: 把建筑物或构筑物推倒、拆开
senses.example: The workers demolished the old warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 工人拆掉了那座旧仓库。
senses.why: An excavator arm against a brick wall.
senses.whyCN: 一条撞上砖墙的挖掘机臂杆。

senses.title: Destroy an argument
senses.definition: to prove an argument or theory completely wrong
senses.definitionCN: 证明一个论点或理论完全错误
senses.example: She demolished his claim with one figure.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个数字就推翻了他的说法。
senses.why: A single number crossing out a whole page.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字划掉整页文字。

senses.title: Defeat completely
senses.definition: to defeat an opponent very easily and heavily
senses.definitionCN: 轻松而沉重地击败对手
senses.example: The champions demolished the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队把客队打得溃不成军。
senses.why: A scoreboard with a gap of forty points.
senses.whyCN: 一块分差四十分的记分牌。

senses.title: Eat up quickly
senses.definition: to eat something quickly and completely, informally
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：很快把东西吃光
senses.example: He demolished the whole pizza.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整个比萨吃光了。
senses.why: An empty plate with only crumbs left.
senses.whyCN: 一个只剩碎屑的空盘。

intro.en: Demolish comes from Latin demoliri, de- plus moliri, to build, from moles, a mass: to bring the mass down.
intro.cn: demolish 源自拉丁语 demoliri，由 de- 加 moliri（建造）构成，moliri 来自 moles（大块）：把大块推下去。

items.en: Moles meant a mass or a huge structure.
items.cn: moles 意为大块、巨大建筑。

items.en: Moliri meant to build or to strive.
items.cn: moliri 意为建造、奋力做。

items.en: Demoliri meant to pull a structure down.
items.cn: demoliri 意为把建筑推倒。

items.en: Demolish entered English for razing buildings.
items.cn: 十六世纪 demolish 以拆毁建筑义进入英语。

items.en: It widened to destroying arguments.
items.cn: 十九世纪扩展到推翻论点。

items.en: Sport and informal speech use it for heavy defeat and eating.
items.cn: 体育与口语用它指大胜与吃光。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the mol- mass family; the near-meaning group names other ways of bringing something down.
note.cn: 形近组共享 mol-（大块）家族；近义组是其他「推倒」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of pulling down a building.
To bother or assault someone.
The smallest unit of a chemical substance.
To damage something so that it no longer exists.
To destroy a building completely.
To show that a claim is false.
To knock something down to the ground.

normalIntro.en: Demolish is de- down plus mol- mass: the mass that was built is brought back down.
normalIntro.cn: demolish 就是 de-（向下）加 mol-（大块）：建起来的大块被推回地面。

normal.en: Mol- means a mass, as in molecule.
normal.cn: mol- 意为大块，如 molecule。

normal.en: De- means down.
normal.cn: de- 表示向下。

normal.en: Demolish a wall and only rubble is left.

senses.title: Show how something works

senses.whyCN: 眼睛看懂的东西，比一页文字来得快。

intro.en: Demonstrate comes from Latin monstrare, to show, with de- adding force; it entered English through the schools.
intro.cn: demonstrate 来自拉丁语 monstrare（展示），前缀 de- 加强语气，经学术用语进入英语。

items.en: Monstrare meant to point out or show, and de- added force to it.
items.cn: monstrare 意为指出或展示，de- 给它加上力度。

items.en: Scholars used demonstrare for proving a point by clear signs.
items.cn: 学者用 demonstrare 表示以清楚的迹象证明一点。

items.en: English took demonstrate for showing a fact by argument or experiment.
items.cn: 英语借来 demonstrate，指用论证或实验展示一个事实。

items.en: The sense of marching in public grew with mass politics.
items.cn: 随着大众政治兴起，走上街头这一层意思长了出来。

items.en: It now covers proof, teaching and street protest alike.
items.cn: 如今它同时覆盖证明、教学与街头抗议。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the demonstr- stem, and the meaning group moves from showing to proving to protesting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 demonstr- 这个词干，近义组则从展示走到证明，再走到抗议。

definition_en: the number below the line in a fraction, which names the size of the parts, or a shared basis for comparison
core_image: 分数横线下方的数字被蓝笔圈出，像给每一份贴上规格标签
scene: 分数横线下方的数字被蓝笔圈出，旁边画着一块被平分的小方块。The denominator names the size of each part in the fraction.
sceneCN: 这里 denominator 指「分数中写在横线下方的数，说明每份的大小」（第 1 个义项：分数的分母）；句意为分母给这个分数里每一份的大小命名。图中可辨识物件：分数横线、蓝笔圈、被平分的小方块、上下两个数字。

pos.zh: 分母；除数；比的后项；共同点

senses.title: The number below the fraction bar
senses.definition: the number in a fraction that names the size of each equal part
senses.definitionCN: 分数中给每个等份的大小命名的那个数
senses.example: The denominator names the size of each part in the fraction.
senses.exampleCN: 分母给这个分数里每一份的大小命名。
senses.why: denominator is Latin for 'namer': the bottom number names what kind of part is being counted, thirds or fifths.
senses.whyCN: denominator 在拉丁语里是「命名者」：下面那个数命名被数的是几分之几。

senses.title: The divisor in a division
senses.definition: the quantity by which another quantity is divided
senses.definitionCN: 用来去除另一个量的那个量
senses.example: In the long division, the denominator stands outside the bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 在竖式除法里，除数写在除号外面。
senses.why: a fraction is a division written down, so the bottom number plays exactly the role of the divisor.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是写下来的除法，因此下面那个数扮演的正是除数的角色。

senses.title: The second term of a ratio
senses.definition: the second quantity named when two amounts are compared as a ratio
senses.definitionCN: 两个量作比时后说出的那个量
senses.example: In the ratio, the denominator is the whole to which the part is compared.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个比里，后项是被拿去比较的那一整个。
senses.why: a ratio is a fraction put into words, so the second term takes the seat of the bottom number.
senses.whyCN: 比就是用文字说出的分数，因此后项坐的就是下面那个数的位置。

senses.title: A common denominator as a shared basis
senses.titleCN: 引申义：共同点、共同基础
senses.definition: a feature shared by different things that makes them comparable
senses.definitionCN: 不同事物共有、使它们可以相互比较的特征
senses.example: A love of cheap travel was the common denominator of the group.
senses.exampleCN: 喜欢便宜的旅行是这个群体的共同点。
senses.why: fractions can only be added when they share a denominator, so the shared bottom number became a metaphor for shared ground.
senses.whyCN: 分数只有在分母相同时才能相加，于是共同的下面那个数成了「共同基础」的比喻。

senses.title: The least common denominator
senses.definition: the smallest number that can serve as the denominator of two or more fractions
senses.definitionCN: 能同时作为两个或更多分数分母的最小那个数
senses.example: Finding the least common denominator made the addition simple.
senses.exampleCN: 找到最小公分母让加法变简单了。
senses.why: the smallest shared bottom number is the practical choice when fractions must be combined, so it has its own fixed name.
senses.whyCN: 分数必须合并时，最小的共同下面那个数就是实用选择，因此它有自己的固定名称。

senses.title: The population at risk in a rate
senses.definition: the total number of people or items over which an event count is divided
senses.definitionCN: 用来除事件计数的那个总人数或总物件数
senses.example: The denominator of the death rate is the whole population at risk.
senses.exampleCN: 死亡率的分母是处在风险中的全部人口。
senses.why: a rate is events over population, and the population below the line is literally the denominator.
senses.whyCN: 率就是事件数除以人口数，写在横线下方的人口就是字面意义上的分母。

senses.title: The denominator polynomial
senses.titleCN: 代数分式的分母多项式
senses.definition: the polynomial written below the line in an algebraic fraction
senses.definitionCN: 代数分式中写在横线下方的那个多项式
senses.example: A zero of the denominator polynomial leaves the expression without a value.
senses.exampleCN: 分母多项式的零点会让表达式没有可取的值。
senses.why: algebraic fractions copy ordinary fractions, so the bottom polynomial keeps the name of the bottom number.
senses.whyCN: 代数分式照搬普通分数，因此下面那个多项式沿用下面那个数的名字。

senses.title: Rationalizing the denominator
senses.definition: the operation of removing a root or irrational number from the bottom of a fraction
senses.definitionCN: 把根号或无理数从分数下方去掉的运算
senses.example: Rationalizing the denominator made the exact value easier to read.
senses.exampleCN: 有理化分母后，精确值更容易读出来。
senses.why: the operation is named after the part it cleans, the denominator at the bottom of the fraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个运算以它清理的那一部分命名，也就是分数下方的分母。

senses.title: An older word for a namer
senses.definition: an older use for a person or thing that gives a name
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指给事物定名的人或物
senses.example: In the old text, the denominator of each district was the clerk who named it.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧文献里，每个辖区的命名者就是给它定名的书记。
senses.why: Latin denominare meant 'to name', and the agent noun kept that literal sense long before fractions adopted it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 denominare 意为「命名」，这个施动名词在分数借用它之前很久就保留着这个字面义。

intro.en: Denominator comes from Latin denominare 'to name', built on de- plus nomen 'name'. The fraction sense arrives through French dénominateur, because the bottom number names the kind of part.
intro.cn: denominator 来自拉丁 denominare「命名」，由 de- 加 nomen「名字」构成。分数义经法语 dénominateur 而来，因为下面那个数为「哪一种份」命名。

items.en: Nomen meant 'name'. It is the source of nominal, nomination, misnomer and the nomen in denominator.
items.cn: nomen 意为「名字」。它是 nominal、nomination、misnomer 的来源，也是 denominator 里的那个 nomen。

items.en: Nominare meant 'to name, call', a verb formed on nomen; its compounds name things in many directions.
items.cn: nominare 意为「命名、称呼」，由 nomen 构成的动词；它的复合形式向多个方向给事物命名。

items.en: De- plus nominare gave denominare 'to name, designate', with the prefix adding completion or specification.
items.cn: de- 加 nominare 构成 denominare「命名、指称」，前缀增添「彻底、具体化」的意思。

items.en: French formed dénominateur for the bottom number of a fraction, since that number names what size the parts are.
items.cn: 法语构成 dénominateur，指分数下面那个数，因为这个数命名每份的大小。

items.en: English adopted denominator in the sixteenth century, and the figurative 'common denominator' followed as fractions became everyday knowledge.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪接受了 denominator，随着分数成为常识，比喻义的「共同点」也随后出现。

items.en: The exact first citation for the figurative sense is approximate; nomen and nominare are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 比喻义的最早确切书证为约数；nomen 与 nominare 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for name and is easy to confuse; the second group names the other parts of a division or ratio.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「名字」的拉丁词，容易混淆；第二组是除法或比里的其他部分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give a name or express in a unit; it is an action, not the bottom number.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为命名或以某单位表示；是动作，不是下面那个数。

entries.definition: A name, a religious body, or a unit value of money; it never means the bottom of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指名称、教派或货币面额；从不指分数的下方。

entries.definition: In name only, or stated rather than real; it keeps nomen without the de- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指名义上的或标称的；保留 nomen 但没有那个表示「离开」的前缀。

entries.definition: A wrong or unsuitable name; it is built on nomen and names a naming error, not a fraction part.
entries.definitionCN: 指错误或不恰当的名称；由 nomen 构成，命名的是命名错误，不是分数的部分。

entries.definition: The top number, built on numerus 'number'; it counts parts while the denominator names them.
entries.definitionCN: 上面那个数，建立在 numerus「数」上；它负责数份数，而分母负责命名。

entries.definition: The number by which another is divided; in a fraction it is the number below the bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来除的那个数；在分数里就是横线下方的数。

entries.definition: The second term of a ratio, matching the denominator's position.
entries.definitionCN: 指比的后项，对应分母的位置。

entries.definition: A foundation or starting value; a common denominator is a figurative base for comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 指基础或起始值；公分母是用于比较的比喻性基础。

entries.definition: A standard used to judge; a common denominator is a shared feature, not a rule of judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于判断的标准；公分母是共有特征，不是判断规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root and suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根与后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: nomen 'name' plus de- plus -ator: the namer at the bottom tells you what kind of part it is.
normal.cn: nomen「名字」加 de- 与 -ator：下面那个命名者告诉你这是几分之几。

normal.en: The family runs denominator, denominate, denomination, nominal and misnomer, all from nomen.
normal.cn: 同族词有 denominator、denominate、denomination、nominal 与 misnomer，都出自 nomen。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: common denominator, least common denominator, rationalize the denominator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：公分母、最小公分母、有理化分母。

normal.en: The denominator names; the numerator counts. Name below, count above.
normal.cn: 分母负责命名，分子负责数数：名字在下，数在上。

normal.en: Two fractions can only be added when their denominators agree, which is why shared ground is called common.
normal.cn: 两个分数只有分母一致才能相加，这就是「共同基础」被称作「公」的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting a cake into equal slices and writing the slice size on each one.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀把蛋糕切成等份，并在每一片上写出这一份的大小。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of strangers who all discover they speak the same language.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子陌生人忽然发现彼此说同一种语言。

abstract.cn: 想象一群人被拿去与整个镇子相比，镇子的数目写在横线下方。

examples.en: A fraction with zero as its denominator is not defined.
examples.cn: 分母为零的分数没有定义。

examples.en: The two groups were compared on a common denominator of income.
examples.cn: 这两个群体按收入的共同基础来比较。

examples.en: Rationalizing the denominator removed the root from the bottom.
examples.cn: 有理化分母把根号从下方去掉了。

root: 拉丁 nomen「名字」→ nominare「命名」→ denominare「定名」→ 法语 dénominateur（分数下方的命名者）→ 英语 denominator。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one role: the number or feature that names the size of the parts. It names parts of a fraction, the divisor, the second term of a ratio, a shared basis, a population base, a polynomial and a cleaned root.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都保留同一个角色：为「每一份有多大」命名的那一个数或特征。它命名分数的份、除数、比的后项、共同基础、人口基数、多项式，以及被清理掉的根号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the number below the fraction bar, circled in blue like a label on each slice.
core.cn: 核心意象：分数横线下方的数，被蓝笔圈住，像每一份上的规格标签。

branches.en: THE NAMING NUMBER: the bottom number tells you the size of each part.
branches.cn: 命名的数：下面那个数告诉你每一份有多大。

branches.en: THE SAME ROLE ELSEWHERE: the divisor of a division and the second term of a ratio.
branches.cn: 同一角色在别处：除法的除数与比的后项。

branches.en: SHARED GROUND: a common bottom number, and the smallest one that two fractions can share.
branches.cn: 共同基础：共同的下面数，以及两个分数能共用的最小那个。

branches.en: WHAT THE LINE DIVIDES BY: the population at risk in a rate, and the polynomial below an algebraic fraction.
branches.cn: 横线用来除什么：比率中的风险人口，以及代数分式下方那个多项式。

branches.en: CLEANING AND NAMING: rationalizing removes a root from the bottom, while the oldest sense is a person who names.
branches.cn: 清理与命名：有理化把根号从下方去掉，而最古老的义项是给人定名的人。

intro.en: Denominator is a Latin agent noun on a verb of naming; its root, prefix and suffix all build English words.
intro.cn: denominator 是建立在「命名」动词上的拉丁施动名词；其词根、前缀与后缀都构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen gives nominal, nomination, misnomer and denomination; the prefix de- and the agent ending -tor complete the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nomen 衍生 nominal、nomination、misnomer 与 denomination；前缀 de- 与施动词尾 -tor 补全了这个词。

pos.zh: 表示；标示；意味着；指代
（符号、词语）表示……的意思

senses.title: Mark off: single a thing out by a mark
senses.titleCN: 划界标出：用标记把某物单独圈出来
senses.definition: to mark something off from others, or identify it by a distinguishing mark
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从其他事物中划出来，或用有区别的标记把它认出来
senses.example: On the plan, each plot is denoted by a small numbered square.
senses.exampleCN: 在平面图上，每一块地都用带编号的小方框标出。
senses.why: Latin denotare joins de- 'completely' to notare 'to mark'. The first English sense in the 1590s was 'mark off from others; identify by a mark' — the mark does not describe the thing, it singles it out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 denotare 由 de-“完全”加 notare“做标记”构成。16 世纪 90 年代英语最早的意思是“把某物从别的东西里划出来、用标记认出它”——标记不描写事物，只把它单独点出来。

senses.title: Be the sign of: stand in place of something
senses.titleCN: 标示：作为某物的记号站在那里
senses.definition: to be a sign or symptom of something; to indicate it
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事物的记号或征兆；表明、指示该事物
senses.example: The raised flag denotes that the track is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 升起的旗子表示这条跑道已关闭。
senses.why: Once a mark can single a thing out, the mark can also stand for it. The 1590s record already includes 'be the sign or symptom of', so the physical mark became a sign read by an observer.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个标记能把事物单独点出来，它也能代替那个事物站在那里。16 世纪 90 年代的记录已含“是……的记号或征兆”，于是手上的标记变成了让观察者去读的符号。

senses.title: Of a word: carry a literal meaning
senses.titleCN: 字面所指：一个词承载的本义
senses.definition: of a word, to have a particular literal meaning or refer to a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 指词语具有某种字面意义，或指称某一特定事物
senses.example: In British English, 'flat' denotes an apartment, not a tyre.
senses.exampleCN: 在英式英语里，flat 指的是公寓，而不是轮胎。
senses.why: Language took the sign relation and made it verbal: a word is the mark, its literal meaning is what the mark stands for. This is the 'denotation' later contrasted with the feelings a word carries.
senses.whyCN: 语言把“记号—所指”这层关系搬到了词语上：词是标记，字面意义是标记所代表的东西。这就是后来与“言外之感”相对立的“外延、字面意义”。

senses.title: Of a symbol: represent a fixed value
senses.titleCN: 符号代表：固定地代表某个对象
senses.definition: of a symbol, to represent or stand for a particular object or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 指符号代表、指代某一特定对象或数量
senses.example: In the equation, the letter x denotes an unknown number.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，字母 x 表示一个未知数。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the strictest part of the word: a symbol is appointed to stand for exactly one value. The mark is arbitrary, but the standing-for is fixed by rule.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了这个词最严格的一面：一个符号被指定代表恰好一个值。记号本身是任意的，但“代表什么”由规则固定下来。

senses.title: Point to indirectly: suggest without saying
senses.titleCN: 暗示：不直说而指向某意
senses.definition: to suggest or imply something indirectly, rather than state it openly
senses.definitionCN: 间接地暗示或意味着某事，而不是公开说出
senses.example: A rising tone may denote doubt rather than a real question.
senses.exampleCN: 升调可能表示怀疑，而不是真正的提问。
senses.why: A sign need not be explicit. Since a mark can be read for what it hints at, denote widened from 'stand for' to 'point toward' — the listener infers what the sign implies.
senses.whyCN: 记号不必明说。既然一个标记可以被读出它暗示的东西，denote 就从“代表”扩大到“指向”——听者去推断记号所隐含的意思。

senses.title: Denotation in semantics: the hard edge of meaning
senses.titleCN: 语义学的外延：意义中坚硬的那条边
senses.definition: in semantics, the direct or literal meaning of an expression, as opposed to its connotation
senses.definitionCN: 语义学中指表达式的直接或字面意义，与内涵、联想义相对
senses.example: The denotation of 'snake' is a reptile; its connotation may be danger.
senses.exampleCN: snake 的外延是一种爬行动物；它的内涵可能是危险。
senses.why: Twentieth-century linguistics split the old verb into two nouns: denotation is what the sign covers, connotation is what it trails behind. The term keeps the word's original 'marking out' image.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪语言学把这个旧动词拆成两个名词：外延是符号所覆盖的范围，内涵是它身后拖着的联想。术语仍保留这个词最初“划出范围”的意象。

senses.title: Of a name: designate a person or office
senses.titleCN: 指称：名称指定某个人或职位
senses.definition: of a name or title, to designate a particular person, group, or office
senses.definitionCN: 指名称或头衔指定某个人、群体或职位
senses.example: 'Chair' denotes the person who runs the meeting, not the furniture.
senses.exampleCN: chair 指的是主持会议的人，而不是那件家具。
senses.why: A title is a mark pinned on a person. The 'mark off' sense survives here: the name does not describe the holder, it identifies which person is meant.
senses.whyCN: 头衔是别在人身上的标记。“划出来”的义项在这里仍然活着：名称不描写持有者，只指明说的是哪一个人。

senses.title: In medicine: be a symptom of
senses.titleCN: 医学上：作为某种病症的指征
senses.definition: of a symptom or test result, to indicate the presence of a particular disease or condition
senses.definitionCN: 指症状或检查结果表明存在某种疾病或状况
senses.example: A persistent cough may denote a lung infection.
senses.exampleCN: 持续咳嗽可能表明肺部感染。
senses.why: Medicine uses the body as a surface of signs. A symptom marks a hidden condition the way a flag marks a closed track; the visible sign denotes what cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 医学把身体当作一片符号的表面。症状标示看不见的病情，就像旗子标示关闭的跑道；可见的征兆代表着看不见的东西。

senses.title: In grammar: a form marks a function
senses.titleCN: 语法上：形式标记某一功能
senses.definition: of a grammatical form, to signal a particular function such as tense, number, or case
senses.definitionCN: 指语法形式标示时态、数、格等特定功能
senses.example: In English, the -s ending denotes plural number on nouns.
senses.exampleCN: 在英语里，-s 词尾表示名词的复数。
senses.why: Grammarians treat inflection as a mark on a stem. The suffix is the visible mark; plural is the function it denotes, so the 1590s 'mark' sense is applied to the smallest pieces of language.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家把屈折变化看作词干上的标记。后缀是看得见的记号，复数是它所表示的功能——16 世纪 90 年代那个“标记”义就这样用到了语言最小的部件上。

intro.en: Denote comes from Latin denotare, 'mark out, designate', built from de- 'completely' and notare 'to mark'. It reached English through French dénoter in the 1590s, and later became a technical term in logic and semantics.
intro.cn: denote 来自拉丁语 denotare“标出、指定”，由 de-“完全”与 notare“做标记”构成。它经法语 dénoter 于 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语，后来成为逻辑学和语义学的术语。

items.en: Denotare meant 'to mark out, point out, designate'. It is a transparent compound of de- 'completely' and notare 'to mark', from nota 'a mark, sign, note'.
items.cn: denotare 意为“标出、指出、指定”，是 de-“完全”与 notare“做标记”的透明复合词，而 notare 来自 nota“标记、符号、记号”。

items.en: French dénoter carried the Latin sense 'to denote, mark out' and supplied the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 法语 dénoter 承袭拉丁语“标示、标出”的意思，并提供了英语借入的词形。

items.en: The first English records give 'mark off from others; identify by a mark; be the sign or symptom of'. The mark and the thing it stands for arrive together.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“把某物从其他事物中划出；用标记辨认；是……的记号或征兆”。标记与它所代表的事物是一起出现的。

items.en: The verb settled into the general sense 'be a sign of, indicate'. Objects, words, and symptoms could all denote what they pointed to.
items.cn: 这个动词稳定在泛指的“是……的记号、表明”上。物件、词语、症状都可以 denote 它们所指向的东西。

items.en: Logic and linguistics turned denote into a technical word: denotation is the literal range of a term, while connotation is the feeling it drags along. The spelling and the mark image have not changed.
items.cn: 逻辑学和语言学把 denote 变成术语：denotation 是词语的字面范围，connotation 是它拖着的感受。拼写与“标记”的意象都没有变。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to move someone to a lower rank or position. It shares the de- opening and the stress pattern of denote.
entries.definitionCN: 使降级、降职。与 denote 同样以 de- 开头、重音位置相同。

entries.definition: to give one's time or energy wholly to something. It differs from denote by a single consonant.
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或精力完全献给某事。与 denote 只差一个辅音。

entries.definition: to publicly declare someone or something wrong or evil. It begins with the same deno- string but ends in a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 公开谴责、告发。开头同样是 deno-，但词根不同。

entries.definition: to have a particular sense or refer to a particular thing. It is the plain everyday match for denote in its word sense.
entries.definitionCN: 意思是；指的是。对应 denote 表“词语字面意义”的义项，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: to be a sign of something, or to make a meaning known. It is close to denote but often implies communication.
entries.definitionCN: 表示；意味着；象征。与 denote 接近，但更强调传达出意思。

entries.definition: to show or point to something, often indirectly. It matches the 'be a sign of' sense without the technical weight.
entries.definitionCN: 表明；指示。对应“是……的记号”义，但没有术语色彩。

entries.definition: to stand for something or act on its behalf. It matches denote in the symbol-and-name senses.
entries.definitionCN: 代表；象征。对应 denote 的符号义和名称指称义。

entries.definition: to be an abbreviation or symbol of something. It is the spoken paraphrase of what a mark denotes.
entries.definitionCN: 代表；是……的缩写或符号。是“一个标记 denote 什么”的口语说法。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin notare family behind note and notify, the con- prefix inside connote, and the everyday habit of reading marks as signs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：note、notify 背后拉丁语 notare 词族，connote 里的 con- 前缀，以及人把标记读成符号的日常习惯。

normal.en: de- means 'completely' and notare means 'to mark': to denote is to mark a thing fully, so that the mark can stand for it.
normal.cn: de- 是“完全”，notare 是“做标记”：denote 就是把标记完整地打在事物上，好让这个标记能代替它。

normal.en: note, notable, notify and denote all sit on Latin nota 'mark'. A note is a mark you make so the thing can be found again.
normal.cn: note、notable、notify、denote 都站在拉丁语 nota“标记”上。note 是你做的标记，为的是以后还能找到那件事。

normal.en: connote = con- 'with' + notare 'mark': connotation is the extra mark a word carries along with its plain denotation.
normal.cn: connote = con-“一起”+ notare“标记”：connotation 就是一个词在字面外延之外顺带带着的额外标记。

normal.en: In a dictionary, the denotation is the first line; the connotation is what the usage note whispers after it.
normal.cn: 词典里，denotation 是第一行释义；connotation 是后面用法说明悄悄补充的那层意味。

normal.en: Mathematicians say x denotes a number: the letter is a mark appointed to stand in the number's place.
normal.cn: 数学家说 x denotes 一个数：字母是被指派站在那个数位置上的标记。

abstract.en: A sign is a finger pointing at the moon: denote gives the pointing, not the moonlight.
abstract.cn: 符号是指向月亮的手指：denote 给出的是那根手指，而不是月光。

abstract.en: Denotation is the hard edge of a word's meaning; connotation is the soft shadow it casts.
abstract.cn: 外延是词义坚硬的那条边，内涵是它投下的柔软影子。

abstract.en: To denote is to draw a line around a thing and say: this mark, and no other, stands here.
abstract.cn: denote 就是绕着事物画一条线，然后说：站在这里的，是这个标记，不是别的。

examples.en: In this chart, the red bars denote last year's sales.
examples.cn: 在这张图里，红色柱条表示去年的销售额。

examples.en: For many people, a wedding ring denotes commitment rather than wealth.
examples.cn: 对许多人来说，婚戒表示的是承诺，而不是财富。

examples.en: The symbol @ denotes 'at' in an email address.
examples.cn: 符号 @ 在电子邮件地址中表示“at”。

dict_mnemonic.text: “点 note”——de（完全）+ note（标记），把标记完全点到事物上，就是标示、表示

root: 源自拉丁语 denotare“标出、指定”，由 de-“完全”+ notare“做标记”构成，notare 又来自 nota“标记”；经法语 dénoter 于 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of denote, from a mark that singles a thing out to the semantic term for literal meaning. Each step keeps the same move: a visible mark is placed where something else should be read.
sensesIntro.cn: denote 的九个义项，从把事物单独划出的标记，一直到语义学里指“字面意义”的术语。每一步都保持同一个动作：把一个看得见的标记放在本该读出别的东西的位置上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark laid on a thing so that the mark can stand for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一个标记打在事物上，好让这个标记代替它。

branches.en: THE MARK AND THE SIGN: first the mark identifies a thing, then the same mark is read as its sign.
branches.cn: 标记与符号：先是用标记认出事物，接着同一个标记被读成事物的符号。

branches.en: WORDS AND NAMES: a word marks a literal meaning, and a title marks which person is meant.
branches.cn: 词与名称：词标出字面意义，头衔标出说的是哪个人。

branches.en: FORMAL MARKS: a mathematical symbol stands for a fixed value, and a grammatical ending marks a function.
branches.cn: 形式标记：数学符号代表固定数值，语法词尾标示功能。

branches.en: READING BEYOND THE MARK: a tone hints at doubt, and a symptom points to a hidden disease.
branches.cn: 读出标记之外：语调暗示怀疑，症状指向看不见的疾病。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL EDGE: denotation names the literal range of a term, set against its connotation.
branches.cn: 术语的边界：外延命名词语的字面范围，与内涵相对。

intro.en: Denote is a Latin loan built on the stem not- 'mark': note, notable, notify and annotate share it, while de-, con- and ad- change the direction of the marking.
intro.cn: denote 是建立在词干 not-“标记”上的拉丁借词：note、notable、notify、annotate 共用这个词干，而 de-、con-、ad- 改变标记的方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin nota 'mark, sign' produces notare 'to mark', then denotare 'mark out', annotare 'write down beside', and connote 'mark along with'. The family is about marks, not about knowledge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nota“标记、符号”生出 notare“做标记”，再生成 denotare“标出”、annotare“在旁边写下”、connotare“连带着标记”。这个词族讲的是标记，不是知识。

items.meaning: to mark out; be a sign of
items.meaningCN: 标示；表示（de- 完全 + notare 标记）
items.example: The crest denotes the city's founding family.
items.exampleCN: 这个纹章标示这座城市的创建家族。

items.meaning: the literal meaning or range of a term
items.meaningCN: 字面意义；外延（-ation 构成名词）
items.example: Definitions focus on denotation, not on tone.
items.exampleCN: 释义关注的是字面意义，而不是语气。

items.meaningCN: 指示的；字面意义的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: Scientific writing tends to be denotative.
items.exampleCN: 科学写作倾向于使用字面意义。

items.meaning: a short written record; to notice
items.meaningCN: 笔记；注意到（直接来自 nota 标记）
items.example: She noted the exact time of the call.
items.exampleCN: 她记下了那通电话的确切时间。

items.meaningCN: 值得注意的；显著的（-able 值得）
items.example: The town is notable for its stone bridge.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇因石桥而闻名。

items.example: Please notify us of any change of address.
items.exampleCN: 地址如有变动，请通知我们。

items.meaning: to add notes beside a text
items.meaningCN: 给……作注释（ad- 朝向 + notare 标记）
items.example: Students annotate the poem in the margins.
items.exampleCN: 学生们在页边给这首诗作注释。

items.meaning: a note added to a text
items.meaningCN: 注释；评注（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The annotation explains an old idiom.
items.exampleCN: 这条注释解释了一个古老的习语。

items.meaning: to carry an extra suggested meaning
items.meaningCN: 意味着；含言外之意（con- 一起 + notare 标记）
items.example: The word 'home' connotes warmth and safety.
items.exampleCN: home 这个词含有温暖和安全的意味。

definition_zh: v. 谴责；公开指责；告发；宣布废除（条约）
definition_en: to criticise someone or something publicly and strongly, or to inform against them
core_image: 讲台上的人指着屏幕上的名单逐条念出指控，台下记者的笔尖不停
scene: 部长公开谴责了这次袭击。The minister denounced the attack.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：denounced 指公开谴责；句意是部长公开谴责了这次袭击。

pos.zh: 谴责；公开指责；告发；宣布废除（条约）

senses.title: Criticise publicly
senses.definition: to criticise someone or something strongly in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合强烈批评某人或某事
senses.example: The minister denounced the attack.
senses.exampleCN: 部长公开谴责了这次袭击。
senses.why: A finger pointed at a list on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 一根指着屏幕上名单的手指。

senses.title: Inform against
senses.definition: to tell the authorities about the illegal activity of someone
senses.definitionCN: 向当局举报某人的非法活动
senses.example: He was denounced by a neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 他被一个邻居告发了。
senses.why: A signed note pushed under an office door.
senses.whyCN: 一张从办公室门缝下塞进去的署名纸条。

senses.title: End a treaty
senses.definition: to declare formally that a treaty or agreement is ended
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布条约或协定终止
senses.example: The state denounced the treaty in 1936.
senses.exampleCN: 该国于一九三六年宣布废除该条约。
senses.why: A seal broken on a folded agreement.
senses.whyCN: 一份折好的协定上被破开的印。

intro.en: Denounce comes from Latin denuntiare, de- plus nuntiare, to announce, from nuntius, a messenger.
intro.cn: denounce 源自拉丁语 denuntiare，由 de- 加 nuntiare（宣布）构成，nuntiare 来自 nuntius（信使）。

items.en: Nuntius meant a messenger.
items.cn: nuntius 意为信使。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to announce.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为宣布。

items.en: Denuntiare meant to announce against, to threaten.
items.cn: denuntiare 意为宣告反对、威胁。

items.en: Denounce entered English for proclaiming against.
items.cn: 十三世纪 denounce 以宣告反对义进入英语。

items.en: It came to mean informing against someone.
items.cn: 十五世纪转而指告发某人。

items.en: It is now chiefly public condemnation.
items.cn: 如今主要指公开谴责。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the nounc- announcing family; the near-meaning group names other ways of speaking against.
note.cn: 形近组共享 nounc-（宣布）家族；近义组是其他「反对着说」的方式。

entries.definition: To make something known publicly.
To say a word, or declare formally.
To give up a claim or belief formally.
To express strong disapproval of.
To say that someone has done wrong.
To point out the faults of something.

normalIntro.en: Denounce is de- against plus nounc- announce: to announce something against a person.
normalIntro.cn: denounce 就是 de-（反对）加 nounc-（宣布）：对着一个人宣布坏话。

normal.en: Nounc- means to announce, as in announce.
normal.cn: nounc- 意为宣布，如 announce。

normal.en: De- here means against.
normal.cn: 这里 de- 表示反对。

normal.en: Denounce the attack means condemn it publicly.
normal.cn: denounce the attack 指公开谴责袭击。

normal.en: To denounce a neighbour is to inform on him.
normal.cn: denounce 一个邻居就是告发他。

normal.en: A state can denounce a treaty.
normal.cn: 一个国家可以宣布废除条约。

examples.cn: 这篇演说抨击了职务腐败。

examples.en: They are denouncing the new law.
examples.cn: 他们正在谴责这项新法律。

dict_mnemonic.text: denounce 谐音「弟闹死」——不如记 de（向下、反对）＋ nounce（宣布，与 announce 同根 nuntius 信使）＝对着某人宣布坏话，「谴责、告发」。

root: 拉丁语 nuntius（信使）→ nuntiare（宣布）→ de-＋nuntiare → denuntiare（宣告反对）→ 英语 denounce

sensesIntro.en: One announcement against: a speech, a note and a broken seal.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次反对的宣告：一篇演说、一张纸条与一枚破开的印。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker reading charges from a list on a screen while reporters write below
core.cn: 核心意象：讲台上的人指着屏幕上的名单逐条念出指控，台下记者的笔尖不停

branches.en: A finger pointed at a list on a screen.
branches.cn: 一根指着屏幕上名单的手指。

branches.cn: 一份折好的协定上被破开的印。

branches.en: Both name someone as being in the wrong.
branches.cn: 两者都指认某人有错。

branches.en: Both are formal acts addressed to an authority.
branches.cn: 两者都是面向权威方的正式行为。

intro.en: Denounce is de- plus nounc-; the messenger root builds the announcing family.
intro.cn: denounce 由 de- 加 nounc- 构成；信使这个词根造出宣布一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntius means a messenger, nuntiare to announce and damnare to condemn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntius 意为信使，nuntiare 意为宣布，damnare 意为判罪。

definition_zh: 密集的；浓密的；晦涩的
definition_en: with parts packed closely together, thick enough to block light, or hard to read
core_image: 一片树冠层层叠叠，阳光只能漏下几小点
scene: 走进林子深处，枝叶在头顶合拢，光只剩下细碎的斑点。The dense forest kept the midday sun off the ground.
sceneCN: 这里 dense 指「浓密的」（第 1 个义项：东西紧密挤在一起）；句意是浓密的森林把正午阳光挡在地面之外。

pos.zh: 密集的；浓密的；晦涩的

senses.title: Packed closely together
senses.definition: with parts or people close together and little space between
senses.definitionCN: 各部分或人挨得很近、间隙很小的
senses.example: A dense crowd filled the square before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午之前，密集的人群站满了广场。
senses.why: Dense means the space between things has almost disappeared.
senses.whyCN: 密集就是说东西之间的空隙几乎消失了。

senses.title: Thick and hard to see through
senses.definition: so thick that light or sight cannot pass easily
senses.definitionCN: 厚到光线或视线难以穿过的
senses.example: The dense forest kept the midday sun off the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 浓密的森林把正午阳光挡在地面之外。
senses.why: When branches close over your head, the sky becomes a rumour.
senses.whyCN: 枝叶在头顶合拢时，天空就只剩一个传闻。

senses.title: Hard to read or follow
senses.definition: written in words so packed that it is hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 文字过于密集而难以读懂的
senses.example: The report was dense with figures.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告塞满数字，读起来很吃力。
senses.why: When ideas stand shoulder to shoulder, a reader has no room to walk.
senses.whyCN: 念头肩并肩站着时，读者就没有走动的余地。

intro.en: Dense comes straight from Latin densus, meaning thick or crowded, and has kept that shape for centuries.
intro.cn: dense 直接来自拉丁语 densus，意为浓密、拥挤，几个世纪以来形状几乎没变。

items.en: Densus described a thick wood or a crowded rank of soldiers.
items.cn: densus 形容茂密的树林或挤紧的士兵队列。

items.en: Writers used it for fog, hair and anything tightly packed.
items.cn: 作家用它写雾、写头发，也写任何紧密挤在一起的东西。

items.en: English borrowed dense for air, smoke and solid matter.
items.cn: 英语借来 dense，用来写空气、烟与固体。

items.en: Science gave it the precise sense of mass in a space.
items.cn: 科学给了它「单位空间里的质量」这一精确含义。

items.en: It now also describes prose that is packed too tightly to enjoy.
items.cn: 如今它也形容塞得太满、读起来不轻松的散文。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dens- stem, and the meaning group gives three ways of being tightly packed.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dens- 词干，近义组则给出三种「紧密挤在一起」的说法。

entries.definition: the amount packed into a space
in a closely packed way

having a large distance between two sides
full of people or things
pressed into a small space

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with leaves closing over a path and end with a page that gives the eye no rest.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从合拢在小路上方的树叶开始，落到一页让眼睛歇不下来的文字。

normal.en: In a dense wood the sky comes to you in pieces.
normal.cn: 在茂密的林子里，天空是一小块一小块来的。

normal.en: Dense fog makes a familiar street into a stranger.
normal.cn: 浓雾能把熟悉的街道变成陌生人。

normal.en: A dense page is a crowd of words with no room to breathe.
normal.cn: 晦涩的一页，是一群没有喘息空间的词。

normal.en: Dense and density differ by a single ending.
normal.cn: dense 与 density 只差一个词尾。

normal.en: Condense is dense with con-, meaning together.
normal.cn: condense 就是 dense 前面加了表示「一起」的 con-。

abstract.en: Picture tree tops touching until the light is only dots.
abstract.cn: 想象树冠彼此相接，光只剩下一粒粒小点。

abstract.en: Picture a bus so full that the door cannot close.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆挤到车门都关不上的公交车。

abstract.en: Picture a paragraph with no white space left.
abstract.cn: 想象一段文字，连一点空白都没剩下。

examples.en: The dense forest kept the midday sun off the ground.
examples.cn: 浓密的森林把正午阳光挡在地面之外。

examples.en: A dense crowd filled the square before noon.
examples.cn: 正午之前，密集的人群站满了广场。

examples.en: The report was dense with figures.
examples.cn: 这份报告塞满数字，读起来很吃力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dense 记成「凳子挤」：想象一排凳子紧紧挨着，中间连脚都插不进去，这就是密集的。

root: 直接来自拉丁语 densus，本义是浓密、拥挤，可形容树林、雾气和挤紧的队列。进入英语后先写空气与固体，十七世纪科学又给了它「单位空间里的质量」这一含义，现代还用它形容过于密集的文字。

sensesIntro.en: From branches closing overhead, to bodies filling a square, to words filling a page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头顶合拢的枝叶，到站满广场的人，再到塞满一页的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaves touching until only dots of light get through.
core.cn: 核心意象：树叶彼此相触，只漏下几点光。

branches.en: The first sense is simple crowding, with no gaps left.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是拥挤，空隙被挤没了。

branches.en: The second sense is thickness that blocks light and sight.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是挡住光线与视线的厚度。

branches.en: The third sense is writing packed until reading becomes work.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是挤到阅读变成体力活的文字。

branches.en: A crowd and a fog both fill space until nothing else fits.
branches.cn: 人群与浓雾都填满空间，直到再塞不进别的。

branches.en: Thick fog and thick prose both leave the reader guessing.
branches.cn: 浓雾与晦涩的文字，都让读者只能猜。

intro.en: Dense has a small Latin family: a noun of measure, an adverb of manner and verbs of pressing together.
intro.cn: dense 有一小族拉丁亲戚：表度量的名词、表方式副词，以及表示压紧的动词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin densus, thick or crowded; con- adds the idea of bringing things together.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 densus（浓密、拥挤），前缀 con- 加上「聚到一起」的意思。

items.example: The fog grew dense near the river.

items.exampleCN: 他们测量了这种液体的密度。

items.example: The denseness of the crowd slowed us.
items.exampleCN: 人群的稠密让我们走得很慢。

items.meaning: to press together or turn to liquid
items.example: Steam condenses on the cold glass.

items.meaning: a device that turns gas into liquid
the change from gas to liquid

items.example: They densified the soil before building.
items.exampleCN: 他们建房前把土压得更实。
